A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
syntactic development may be a by-product of lexical learning.

syntactic abstractions may be formed on the basis of lexical-specific learning, and that the formation of such abstractions may be a crucial mechanism in the transition from the single-word to the multiword stage.
the syntactic abstractions that underlie the development of syntax are formed on the basis of the acquisition of individual lexical items.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the acquisition of syntactic rules is a gradual process in which the children’s learning is guided by the properties of the individual words they know and by the properties of individual constructions they have already acquired.
children’s language acquisition is not a random process, but is guided by general principles that facilitate learning.

children’s early language development can be understood as the result of a process of abstraction, and the emergence of syntactic abstructions is the result of children’s induction from individual word-combination.
